notes.value: Figure 1 is a DFT energy profile, frontier-orbital analysis, and comparison of H2 versus acetic-acid protonation; calculated intermediates/transition states are not isolated experiments.
The calculated pathway starts from dimeric INT1A, forms cationic INT3A and Ni-H INT4A, differentiates (R)-3a/(S)-3a at TS6A-S/TS6A-R, and releases 4a after H2 protonation and ligand exchange.

The source reports TS6A-S versus TS6A-R barriers of 12.7 versus 14.3 kcal/mol relative to INT4A, and TS7A-S versus TS7B-S barriers of 21.6 versus 31.9 kcal/mol; these are calculated energies, not reaction conditions or yields.

unresolved: All Figure 1 species and energies are computational proposals; no independent quantities, experimental yields, observation status, or preparation records belong to them.
The calculation method is described in reference 83 and points to unassociated Supporting Information; no SI detail was imported.

notes.value: Figure 2 is the authors' calculated distortion/interaction stereochemical model; it is not a set of experimental reaction runs.
The model compares directed TS6A-S/TS6A-R, nondirected TS6B-S/TS6B-R, and ethyl-substituted TS6A-S-Et/TS6A-R-Et to rationalize kinetic resolution and the lower s-factors of linear-alkyl substrates.

The page-8/9 discussion states that the combined catalyst/substrate distortion in TS6A-S is 12.2 kcal/mol lower than in TS6A-R and that elevated 70 °C/70 atm experimental conditions can overcome the selectivity barrier; the latter is explanatory context, not a new experiment.
